args.message:
Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money, per FIN-212

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, which fails tests/test_money.py
(e.g. 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66). Fix the nightly build
failure by using ROUND_HALF_EVEN as intended by FIN-212.

args.head: fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`. For example, `2.665` was rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.

## Changes
- Replace `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money()`.

## Testing
- CI run on branch `fin-212-bankers-rounding` (commit 08d3cd5986) passed.

I did not merge, since merging into main requires code-owner approval per policy.

transcript.content: The bug is clear: the implementation uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` (so `2.665` rounds to `2.67`) instead of `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Let me create a branch and fix it.
transcript.reasoning_content: Good catch — 2.675 rounds up to 2.68 under both half-up and half-even (actually 2.675 → 2.68 in both), but 2.665 → 2.66 only under half-even (half-up would give 2.67). Fix the import and rounding mode.
